correctness.rationale: The stated channels give the four ODEs and conserve total mass. The multiplicative equations preserve positivity of X, U and Y at finite time; Z is nondecreasing. Independently differentiating U/√X and Y+U−X/2 gives zero, with respective initial values 1/2 and 1/8. Thus with s=√X−1/2, Y=s²/2 and ds/dt=−s²(1+2s)/4. From s(0)=1/10, s decreases to zero without hitting it at finite time. Then (1/s)'→1/4, so ts→4 and t²Y→8. Conservation gives the other limits; integrating −(log U)'=Y gives log(6/5). This strict algebraic tail precludes any positive exponential upper-bound rate. By the cited definitions the three transition edges are acyclic; the only dependency cycle is X↔Y and Y has persistent successor X (limit 1/4). Proposition 1, Case 1 expressly permits an on-cycle successor. The exhibited strictly positive trajectory is enough to contradict the conjecture as stated, without contradicting the integrability theorem.
residual_risks: The verification is analytic. No claim is made that other initial conditions or nearby parameters exhibit the same decay law.
